newsitem.title: USA: Sylvan to buy National Education for $675 million.
newsitem.headline: Sylvan to buy National Education for $675 million.

text.p: Sylvan Learning Systems Inc., which runs 650 tutoring and trade schools nationwide, has agreed to buy National Education Corp. for about $675 million in stock, the companies said Wednesday.

The deal would create a leading education services company with a national network of schools that serve students of all ages, including adults. It would have combined annual revenues approaching $500 million, the companies said.

Sylvan, known for its Sylvan Learning Centres, said it will issue 0.58 share of its stock for each National Education share. The deal values National Education at $18.34 a share based on Wednesday's prices, the companies said.
Sylvan stock tumbled $5.25 to $29.875 on Nasdaq. National Education closed down 87.5 cents at $16.25.

Analysts said Sylvan shares fell because it was combining with a larger company with a slower growth rate. Sylvan has typically grown earnings per share at 35 percent a year while National Education has grown at 15 percent.
Some said that this ignored the progress made at National Education in boosting its earnings performance in the last two years.
"It is a potential home run, there are tremendous benefits from putting the companies together," said Michael Moe of Montgomery Securities.
"I am favourably inclined to this deal," said Brandt Sakakeeny, an analyst at Smith Barney.

Another analyst, who declined to be identified, noted that news of the deal had clearly leaked out because National Education's stock soared from $12.50 to $17, an almost 50 percent rise, in the week before the deal was announced.

Shareholders of National Education, whose ICS Learning Systems division is the world's largest provider of education through the mail or computers, would hold about 47 percent of the fully diluted common stock of the combined company.

"The combination of our two businesses will create the industry's first true 'life-long learning company' serving education, training and testing needs from kindergarten through high school, to professional education, to advanced degree programmes," said Sam Yau, president of National Education.
The companies said the merger will boost their combined earnings per share in 1997.

"This will place the combined company in an excellent position to increase its business in existing markets and to penetrate new markets within the trillion dollar worldwide education services field," said Doug Becker, Sylvan's chief executive.

Chris Hoehn-Saric, Sylvan's chairman and co-chief executive officer, will serve as chairman of the combined entity. Yau will join Becker as co-chief executive and will manage the acquired operations of National Education.
Sylvan, based in Baltimore, Md., also does computer-based testing for academic admissions and professional licensing programmes and provides educational services to school systems.
It also offers adult education and training and operates Wall Street Institute, a franchisor of English language teaching centres.
Sylvan earned $14.7 million on revenues of $157.1 million in 1996.

National Education provides interactive media-based learning products and owns 83 percent of Steck-Vaughn Publishing Corp., one of the nation's largest publishers of supplemental education materials. Based in Irvine, Calif., it earned $21.4 million on revenues of $288.8 million in 1996.
The deal, approved by the boards of both companies, is subject to approval by regulators and shareholders. It is expected to close by the end of the second quarter.
